diagnosis: Mucinous cystic neoplasm with an associated invasive carcinoma
legend: Lined mostly by high-grade mucinous epithelia. Low-grade mucinous epithelia, ovarian type stroma, and associated invasive carcinoma are seen at 9, 6, and 6 o’clock directions, respectively.
The locules are lined by columnar mucinous epithelium. Note the subepithelial band of hypercellular ovarian-type stroma.

diagnosis: Mucinous cystic neoplasm with an associated invasive carcinoma
legend: The non-invasive component (top) is composed of cysts lined by mucinous epithelium with high-grade dysplasia and subepithelial ovarian-type stroma. The glands of an associated invasive carcinoma are at the bottom.
Macroscopically, mucinous cystic neoplasms typically form unilocular or multilocular cysts containing thick mucin or haemorrhagic material.
The upper locule is lined by epithelium with low-grade dysplasia, while an adjacent locule (below) is lined by epithelium with high-grade dysplasia.
